tour.title: Guided tour
tour.launchUnseen: You have not taken this page's tour yet
tour.overview.name: The Overview
tour.overview.rail.title: The menu down the left
tour.overview.rail.body: Every screen in the app is one of these rows. They are grouped by what you are doing: Operate is what is happening now, Think is goals and decisions, Build is the plumbing, Data is the raw graph, System is settings. Hover a row to see its name; you can hide rows you never use in Settings.
tour.overview.search.title: Search, and jumping between projects
tour.overview.search.body: Click here — or press Ctrl-K (Cmd-K on a Mac) — to search everything: tasks, projects, decisions, people. Press G then P instead and the same box becomes a project switcher, listing the projects you looked at most recently first.
tour.overview.stats.title: These numbers are buttons
tour.overview.stats.body: Overdue, In progress, Done this week, and so on. Click one and the page below narrows to exactly the work it counted — no report opens, you get the actual tasks. Click it again to go back to everything.
tour.overview.lanes.title: What is asking for you today
tour.overview.lanes.body: Four lanes: Critical is late or high priority, In Motion is started, Waiting has not been picked up, Done today is what you finished. Click any task and it opens inside its project with the row highlighted, so you never land on a list wondering which one you clicked.
tour.overview.signals.title: The live feed on the right
tour.overview.signals.body: Everything that has happened recently — a task finished, a build reported back, a rule that fired. Each line is a link to the thing it names. Below it sit your open goals and any decisions still waiting on you.
tour.overview.newProject.title: Start here if the app is empty
tour.overview.newProject.body: A project is a box that holds work. Tasks, labels, sprints, decisions and share links all hang off one, so this is the first thing to make. Give it a name — you can change everything else later.
tour.overview.launcher.title: This button is on every page
tour.overview.launcher.body: Whatever screen you are on, this walks you through it. A dot on it means you have not taken that page's tour yet. Pressing ? does the same thing, and also lists every keyboard shortcut.
tour.overview.guide.title: The written manual
tour.overview.guide.body: The Guide has a chapter per part of the app, with pictures, and a list of every one of these tours so you can take them in order. It is always in the menu — that row cannot be hidden.
tour.project.name: A project
tour.project.progress.title: How much is done
tour.project.progress.body: The bar counts every task in this project, including tasks inside sub-projects nested under it. If some of that work is not in the list below, a line here says how many — that is deliberate, so the number you see is never smaller than the work that exists.
tour.project.newIssue.title: Adding work
tour.project.newIssue.body: This opens a one-line form: a title is all that is required. Priority, due date, labels and who it is for can be filled in now or added later by clicking the task. Pressing C anywhere in the app does the same thing.
tour.project.tabs.title: Five views of the same tasks
tour.project.tabs.body: Issues is the list, with subtasks tucked under their parents. Board is drag-and-drop columns by status. Timeline is a Gantt chart you can drag to change dates. Calendar places each task on its due date. Table is the dense grid for sorting and bulk edits. Nothing is duplicated — it is one set of tasks drawn five ways.
tour.project.filters.title: Narrowing what you see
tour.project.filters.body: Filter by status, priority, label, who it is for, or when it is due, and type in the search box to match titles. The filter stays applied when you switch views, and it is stored in the web address — so you can bookmark a filtered board or send someone the link and they see what you see.
tour.project.rows.title: A task row
tour.project.rows.body: Click the title to edit it in place. The small badges on the right each open a panel: comments, blocked-by dependencies, file attachments, repeat-every-week rules, and build results from your CI. Subtasks appear indented underneath and count as real work everywhere in the app.
tour.project.share.title: Showing this to someone outside
tour.project.share.body: This makes a read-only public web page for the project, with a link anyone can open. You can lock it with a PIN, set a date it stops working, let visitors leave notes, and see how many times it has been viewed. There is also a calendar feed here you can subscribe to from Google Calendar or Apple Calendar.
tour.project.agent.title: Letting an AI agent work here
tour.project.agent.body: This panel gives you the instructions to paste into an AI coding agent so it can read and update this project through the API. Anything you can do on this screen, an agent can do with an API key — the keys are made under System, API Keys.
tour.analytics.name: Analytics
tour.analytics.filters.title: Pick what you are measuring
tour.analytics.filters.body: Leave the first box on All projects for a whole-account picture, or choose one project to unlock its sprint charts. The last box sets how far back the trend lines look: a week, a month or three months.
tour.analytics.cards.title: The headline numbers
tour.analytics.cards.body: Total, done, in progress, and how many are overdue. Overdue means one thing everywhere in this app: past its due date and not finished or failed. A failed task is not late, it is failed, and it is counted under its own heading instead.
tour.analytics.charts.title: The charts, and getting the numbers out
tour.analytics.charts.body: The heatmap shows which days you were busy. Burndown and velocity need a project with sprints selected. Calibration compares the time you estimated against the time things actually took. Each section has a CSV button, so any chart here can be opened in a spreadsheet.
tour.structure.name: The structure map
tour.structure.style.title: Four ways to draw the same thing
tour.structure.style.body: This map shows what lives inside what. Tree nests children under parents, Sankey shows the flow as indented bands, Territory draws children inside their parent's card, and Network is the free-floating web with lines you can follow.
tour.structure.filters.title: Showing less
tour.structure.filters.body: Narrow the map to only active work, only what is at risk, and so on. If a filter hides something that had children, the children move up to the top level rather than vanishing with it — you never lose work by filtering.
tour.structure.stats.title: The count strip
tour.structure.stats.body: How many identities, projects and tasks are on the map, plus what is at risk and what nothing owns. Unowned is worth glancing at: it is work sitting outside any identity.
tour.structure.canvas.title: The map itself
tour.structure.canvas.body: Drag to move around, scroll to zoom, and use the + and - buttons or the fit button to reset. Click a box to select it, double-click to open it. The dashed lines are dependencies — one task waiting on another.
tour.goals.name: Goals
tour.goals.new.title: What a goal is for
tour.goals.new.body: A goal is the outcome you want by a date — 'ship the beta by March' — sitting above the tasks that get you there. Give it a title, a target date, and tick which projects count towards it.
tour.goals.tabs.title: Filtering by state
tour.goals.tabs.body: Active, achieved, missed. The number beside each is how many are in that state, so you can see at a glance whether you are carrying too many at once.
tour.goals.list.title: A goal card
tour.goals.list.body: The bar is progress across every project linked to the goal, counted automatically — you never update it by hand. You can also attach individual tasks straight to the goal from the box at the bottom of the card.
tour.decisions.name: Decisions
tour.decisions.new.title: Writing down why
tour.decisions.new.body: A decision record answers 'why is it like this?' — the question a task list has no place for and someone asks six months later. Write what you chose and what you considered, then set it to proposed, accepted, deprecated, or replaced.
tour.decisions.mode.title: List or graph
tour.decisions.mode.body: The list files decisions under the project and organization they belong to. The graph draws how they relate: an arrow points from a decision to the one it replaces, and work a decision governs sits below it. Click a node in the graph and everything unrelated dims.
tour.decisions.console.title: The scoreboard and filters
tour.decisions.console.body: How many are proposed, accepted, archived, and how many are actively governing work. Proposed is the number that matters day to day — those are decisions still waiting on you.
tour.decisions.groups.title: How records are filed
tour.decisions.groups.body: Grouped by where they live, so an organization holding four projects is one heading you can fold shut, not four. Big sections start collapsed. Each card's ⋯ menu is where you link one decision to another: replaces, requires, or conflicts with.
tour.templates.name: Templates
tour.templates.new.title: Work you set up the same way every time
tour.templates.new.body: A template is a task you keep re-creating — 'onboard a client', 'cut a release' — saved with its subtasks, labels and default priority already filled in. Build it once here.
tour.templates.list.title: Using one
tour.templates.list.body: Apply a template to any project and it creates the task and all of its subtasks in one go. Templates are shared across every project, so you write them once and use them anywhere.
tour.assistant.name: The assistant
tour.assistant.conversations.title: Your conversations
tour.assistant.conversations.body: Each chat is kept and searchable, so you can come back to what the assistant told you last week. The + button starts a fresh one.
tour.assistant.prompts.title: It can actually change things
tour.assistant.prompts.body: Ask it in plain language — 'what is overdue?', 'plan my day', 'make a task to renew the domain'. It reads your real data and can create and update tasks, not just talk about them. The suggested prompts are a starting point. Which AI provider it uses is set in Settings, and takes effect on your next message.
tour.activity.name: Activity
tour.activity.console.title: Filtering the history
tour.activity.console.body: Everything that has ever happened, narrowed to one project or one kind of event. The number beside each type tells you how noisy it is before you click it.
tour.activity.views.title: Three ways to read it
tour.activity.views.body: Timeline spreads events across the last day so you can see bursts. Wall groups them by what happened. Log is the plain reverse-chronological list. Same events, different question.
tour.activity.feed.title: Every line goes somewhere
tour.activity.feed.body: Each entry names a task or project and links to it, so 'what changed?' and 'take me there' are one click apart. This history is never deleted when the thing it describes is — retiring a project does not retire its record.
tour.integrations.name: Integrations
tour.integrations.new.title: Telling something else what happened
tour.integrations.new.body: An integration sends a message out when something changes here — to a Slack or Discord webhook, to any URL, or as an email. Pick which events it cares about and which project, or leave the project blank to hear about everything.
tour.integrations.list.title: Delivery, and why it failed
tour.integrations.list.body: Every attempt is recorded, with retries spaced out over a few hours if the far end is down — a webhook's failure mode is silence, so it is logged rather than assumed. Passwords and tokens you enter here are never sent back to the browser: they read as blank, and leaving them blank means 'leave it as it was'.
tour.rules.name: Automation rules
tour.rules.new.title: If this, then that
tour.rules.new.body: A rule watches for something — a task created, a field changed, a link made between two things — checks the conditions you set, and then acts: change a status, add a label, send a notification. Before you save it, the dry run shows you exactly what it would have done to your real data.
tour.rules.list.title: Reading the counters
tour.rules.list.body: Each rule shows how many times it ran and how many times it actually changed something. Those two numbers being far apart is the case worth looking at: a rule firing constantly and doing nothing looks identical to one that works. Rules never set off other rules.
tour.webhookLogs.name: Delivery log
tour.webhookLogs.filters.title: Finding the failure
tour.webhookLogs.filters.body: Narrow to failed or dead deliveries, or to one integration. Dead means it ran out of retries and gave up.
tour.webhookLogs.table.title: What each row tells you
tour.webhookLogs.table.body: The event, where it was sent, the HTTP code that came back and how many attempts it took. Open a row to see the exact request and response. Any password or token in the headers is blanked out here too.
tour.apiKeys.name: API keys
tour.apiKeys.new.title: Letting a program in
tour.apiKeys.new.body: A key lets scripts and AI agents use this app without a browser. Choose what it may do — read, write, or admin — and optionally lock it to a single project or identity, which limits it to that box and everything inside it.
tour.apiKeys.list.title: The key is shown once
tour.apiKeys.list.body: Copy it when it is created; it is never displayed again. If you lose it, delete the key and make another. Below the list is the address and an example request, so you can test it straight away.
tour.identities.name: Identities
tour.identities.new.title: Keeping several lives apart
tour.identities.new.body: An identity is a hat you wear — work, freelance, a side project, a client. Give it a name, a colour and a letter, and file projects under it. It is a real container, so counts roll up through it.
tour.identities.list.title: What each one holds
tour.identities.list.body: The badge counts projects filed under this identity. The settings button opens sharing for the whole identity at once: a public page, a calendar feed, a PIN, an expiry date.
tour.identities.focus.title: Wearing one at a time
tour.identities.focus.body: This is the switcher up in the menu. Pick an identity and the whole app narrows to its work — the overview, search, the project list. Choose 'no focus' to see everything again. It is one control with as many values as you have identities, which is why there is not a menu row per identity.
tour.explorer.name: The data explorer
tour.explorer.types.title: Everything is a node
tour.explorer.types.body: Underneath, a project, a task, a decision and an identity are all the same thing — a node with a type. This column lists every type with how many exist, and those totals are counted on the server, so the number beside a type is never just the number on this page.
tour.explorer.loose.title: Finding what fell out
tour.explorer.loose.body: Loose means nothing above it and nothing below it: not filed anywhere, and holding nothing. A top-level organization is not loose even though nothing contains it — it holds work. This is the box for things you created and forgot to put anywhere.
tour.explorer.search.title: Search across everything
tour.explorer.search.body: Type to match titles across the selected type, or across all of them. The count line says how many you are looking at out of the type's total, and Load more fetches the next page — nothing is silently cut off.
tour.explorer.detail.title: Connections, and making one
tour.explorer.detail.body: Select a row and this panel lists everything it is connected to, in both directions. The picker below adds a connection, and it only offers ones that will actually work: it asks the server the same question the save does, so you cannot pick a relation that gets silently stored backwards.
tour.graphTypes.name: Item types
tour.graphTypes.nodes.title: Inventing your own kind of item
tour.graphTypes.nodes.body: Add a type — 'client', 'repository', 'invoice' — and give it roles. A type with the task role is a task everywhere: it shows in searches, counts, reminders and the API, not just on a board. A type with the container role can hold other things. You can also declare its fields, which is what the editor on an item's page draws.
tour.graphTypes.edges.title: The kinds of connection
tour.graphTypes.edges.body: Contains means 'lives inside' and is what every progress bar counts through. Owns means 'belongs to' and counts nothing. Each relation says what may sit at either end, and that rule is enforced when you save — the pickers elsewhere in the app are built from these declarations rather than a second copy of them.
tour.settings.name: Settings
tour.settings.preferences.title: How the app looks to you
tour.settings.preferences.body: Light or dark, the language, the accent colour, and which view a project opens in. These are yours and follow your account to any machine you sign in on.
tour.settings.modules.title: Hiding menu rows you never use
tour.settings.modules.body: Turn off the parts of the app you do not need and drag the rest into the order you want. Overview, Guide and Settings cannot be hidden — those are the three you need to find your way back.
tour.settings.calendar.title: Your deadlines in your calendar
tour.settings.calendar.body: This is a subscribe link covering everything with a due date. Paste it into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook and your tasks appear there, updating on their own. Treat it like a password: anyone holding the link can read it.
tour.settings.backup.title: Backups
tour.settings.backup.body: A backup runs automatically once a day and keeps the last few. You can also run one now, download a copy, or restore from one. A downloaded backup is the whole database, keys included — keep it somewhere safe.
tour.settings.llm.title: Which AI the assistant uses
tour.settings.llm.body: Choose the provider, paste an API key and name a model. This is a live setting: the next message you send uses it, with no restart. You can also point it at your own compatible endpoint instead of the vendor's.
tour.guide.name: The guide
tour.guide.chapters.title: The chapters
tour.guide.chapters.body: One per part of the app, in the order worth reading them. The chapter you are on is in the web address, so you can send someone a link to a specific section rather than telling them where to scroll.
tour.guide.tours.title: Every tour, in one list
tour.guide.tours.body: The same walkthroughs you can start from any page, gathered here so you can take them in order. A tick means you have already been through that one — it is a checklist for a first day.
tour.guide.content.title: The chapter itself
tour.guide.content.body: Screenshots are taken from the running app rather than drawn by hand, so a picture here is never of a version that no longer exists. Click any of them to see it full size.
